    from a prefetched relation, or prefetching the same relation multiple times

    save the costly creation of a QuerySet instance.

I have resolved the issue in [related_descriptors.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-xwz56uts/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py).

### Cause
When prefetching related objects via [`ForwardManyToOneDescriptor.get_prefetch_queryset`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-xwz56uts/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L120-L150), [`ReverseOneToOneDescriptor.get_prefetch_queryset`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-xwz56uts/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L365-L382), and [`RelatedManager.get_prefetch_queryset`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-xwz56uts/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L633-L654), iterating over `queryset` evaluates any nested prefetches (or `select_related`) on the inner queryset first, populating the reverse relation cache on `rel_obj`. The loop body then unconditionally overwrote that cached value on `rel_obj` with the parent `instance` from the outer queryset (along with its deferred fields).

### Solution
Check whether the relation is already cached on `rel_obj` (`is_cached(rel_obj)`) before setting the reverse relation cache to `instance` in `get_prefetch_queryset()`.
